economy.summary: Fitzpatrick says lowering the cost of living should be the focus of the 2026 Congress, stating that every bill brought to the floor should be focused on lowering costs for people who need it most. He opposes broad, indiscriminate tariffs that raise costs on American consumers.
economy.short: Prioritizes lowering cost of living; opposes broad consumer-cost-raising tariffs.

taxes.summary: Fitzpatrick voted for the House version of the 2025 budget reconciliation bill, saying he voted to permanently extend middle-class tax cuts and for enhanced small-business tax relief, along with investments in border security and the military.
taxes.short: Supports permanently extending middle-class tax cuts and small-business tax relief.

abortion.summary: Fitzpatrick says he supports Pennsylvania's law permitting abortion up to 24 weeks and afterward when the mother's life or health is in danger. He voted against the Women's Health Protection Act, which would have codified Roe v. Wade federally, and voted for a bill affirming the right to travel across state lines for an abortion.
abortion.short: Supports Pennsylvania's 24-week law; voted against federally codifying Roe.

education.summary: Fitzpatrick supports full funding of Title I of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and of the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act. He introduced the Student Loan Refinancing and Recalculation Act to allow refinancing of student loan interest rates and eliminate origination fees, and backs the College Transparency Act.
education.short: Supports full Title I and IDEA funding; proposes student-loan refinancing.

healthcare.summary: Fitzpatrick voted against final passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in July 2025, saying the Senate's amendments to Medicaid fell short of his standard for protecting his district, and that he had voted to strengthen Medicaid protections in the earlier House version.
healthcare.short: Voted against 2025 reconciliation bill, citing Senate Medicaid amendments.

energy.summary: Fitzpatrick co-introduced the bipartisan MARKET CHOICE Act in May 2025, which would place a fee on carbon emissions and use the revenue to modernize infrastructure. He is a member of the bipartisan Climate Solutions Caucus.
energy.short: Proposes bipartisan carbon-emissions fee funding infrastructure modernization.

guns.summary: Fitzpatrick co-authored the Bipartisan Background Checks Act to require background checks on nearly all gun sales, voted for the 2022 assault weapons ban as one of two House Republicans to do so, and supported passage of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
guns.short: Supports universal background checks; voted for assault weapons ban.

economy.summary: Harvie proposes repealing the Trump administration's tariffs, which he says drive up grocery and energy prices, raising the federal minimum wage, and supporting small businesses with better access to capital. He supports protecting workers' rights to organize and collectively bargain.
economy.short: Proposes repealing tariffs, raising minimum wage, protecting union rights.

taxes.summary: Harvie supports tax relief for middle-class families and proposes closing tax loopholes used by billionaires and corporations so the ultra-wealthy and big businesses pay their fair share.
taxes.short: Supports middle-class tax relief; proposes closing billionaire, corporate loopholes.

abortion.summary: Harvie says abortion is healthcare and that women, not the government, should make their own reproductive healthcare choices. He supports funding Planned Parenthood.
abortion.short: Says abortion is healthcare; supports funding Planned Parenthood.

education.summary: Harvie proposes investing in early childhood education including pre-K and kindergarten, expanding technical and civics education, making college more affordable, and expanding job training and apprenticeship programs.
education.short: Proposes early-childhood investment, affordable college, expanded job training.

healthcare.summary: Harvie proposes protecting Medicare and Medicaid, reversing the healthcare cuts in the 2025 reconciliation law, expanding access to affordable care including dental, vision, and mental health, lowering prescription drug costs, and preventing crushing medical debt.
healthcare.short: Proposes protecting Medicare/Medicaid, lowering drug costs, reversing cuts.

energy.summary: As Bucks County commissioner, Harvie approved the county's first Climate Action Plan and Operations Sustainability Plan, hired the county's first Director of Sustainability, adopted a resolution targeting 100% renewable energy, and helped create an alternative-energy ordinance for municipalities.
energy.short: Approved county climate action plan; backed 100% renewable-energy resolution.

guns.summary: Harvie, a gun owner, supports background checks, barring gun purchases by people on terrorism no-fly lists, and banning assault weapons, saying they have no place on our streets. His campaign platform also calls for increasing local law enforcement funding.
guns.short: Supports background checks, assault-weapons ban, more police funding.
